function: NBEATS predicts OTFS delay-Doppler channel parameters; a dual-branch DNN designs the AP pre-equalization matrix trading symbol MSE against sensing CRLB, so the UAV detects without equalization (pp. 6-8).
system: ISAC-OTFS air-ground downlink: single-antenna AP and single-antenna UAV UE, 2 scatterers, M=N=16, 3 GHz carrier, 15 kHz spacing, speeds up to 95 m/s, no RIS (pp. 3, 9).
method: Supervised NBEATS network (six stacks of three blocks, MSE loss) for channel prediction; dual-branch residual DNN trained offline with the weighted MSE+CRLB objective as loss (pp. 6-9).
data_channel: Ray-tracing channel parameters (delays, Doppler shifts, attenuations) from Wireless InSite for UE trajectories up to 95 m/s: 640 trajectory groups, split 4:1 train/test (p. 9).
test_conditions: Train and test on the same ray-traced dataset (4:1 split of 640 trajectory groups); transmit-power and weight sweeps; no unseen scenario, speed or site reported (pp. 9-12).
baselines: Non-learned: MMSE equalization with perfect CSI. Learned, for channel prediction only: LSTM, PatchTST, Autoformer. Also the proposed pre-equalization with perfect or outdated CSI (pp. 9-10).
metrics: MAPE of predicted channel parameters, communication MSE, sensing CRLB, MSE-CRLB trade-off, complex multiplications at the UE (Figs. 4-8, pp. 10-12).
complexity: UE-side order O(2^o MN) versus O((MN)^3 + 2^o MN) with equalization; complex multiplications cut by over 75% (Fig. 8, pp. 11-12); AP-side network cost not reported.
q1_support: p. 9: "are incorporated into the Wireless Insite [37] software to generate corresponding channels as the dataset"; self-generated ray tracing of the authors' own scenario, not 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 9: "The dataset consists of 640 trajectory groups, which are divided into training and testing sets in a ratio of 4:1"; this is a held-out part of the same data, and the paper reports no unseen scenario, speed or site.
q3_support: p. 9: "the MMSE equalization, which is calculated using the communication channel matrix of perfect CSI, is performed at the UE side" (non-learned, compared on MSE, Figs. 5-7); p. 10: "Fig. 4 compares the accuracy of the NBEATS-based OTFS channel prediction module with the common time-series prediction algorithm" (LSTM, PatchTST, Autoformer, on MAPE).
q4_support: p. 12: "the processing complexity is reduced by more than 75% compared to channel equalization at the UE side"; orders O(2^o MN) versus O((MN)^3 + 2^o MN) and multiplication counts for the proposed framework (pp. 11-12), UE side only.
q5_support: p. 9: "generate corresponding channels as the dataset"; the data are self-generated, and the paper gives no link to code or data (the only URL is the Wireless InSite product page in [37], p. 13).
notes: Step 1: research article; learned NBEATS predictor and dual-branch DNN (pp. 6-8); physical layer. Area 4: OTFS delay-Doppler channel prediction and pre-equalization so that the UAV detects without equalization (p. 1); the system is also ISAC, but area 4 outranks 5 in the tie-break order. The single-antenna AP and UE (p. 3) is admitted for OTFS; had the reviewer placed the work in area 2 or 5, it would fall under the system exclusion. The CSI processing module (channel reconstruction and inversion) is not learned (p. 8). q3 is borderline: the learned baselines (LSTM, PatchTST, Autoformer) are compared on the prediction module only (Fig. 4), and the pre-equalization network has no learned baseline. q4 is borderline: only the UE-side cost is quantified (pp. 11-12); no FLOPs, parameters or runtime for the AP-side networks. q1: Wireless InSite ray tracing of a self-made scenario, not a public dataset; reviewer may confirm. The PDF is the arXiv 2412.04751v2 preprint (p. 1).
